title: Connecting Freelance Platforms (Upwork, Deel, Toptal) to Indian Bank Accounts
summary: Connect Upwork, Deel and Toptal withdrawals to Indian banking. Compare fees, receiving-account rules, remittance documents, EEFC accounts and payout workflows.
body_markdown:

Toggle


A $10,000 invoice paid by your client deducts the same amount from their account. But this full $10,000 won’t reach your account. There are deductions.


The gap between what you bill for and what you receive exists in three places;


- FX Spread
- Withdrawal Fee
- Paperwork hole


Most freelancers only account for the first gap and rarely do they notice the third one. They find this gap when claiming to get a GST refund.


We aim to address this disconnect between your expectations and reality. As a freelancer, connecting freelance platforms to the Indian banking system needs strict treasury architecture and not just PayPal or[SWIFT](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/swift-money-transfer/) configurations.


### Key Takeaways


- Check Upwork, Deel or Toptal’s available withdrawal methods before connecting a receiving account. Cashfree compatibility needs confirmation.
- Compare the exchange rate, platform charges, provider fees and taxes using the final INR amount received.
- Keep invoices and remittance records together. An INR credit or missing MT103 does not automatically decide GST export status.
- EEFC accounts and domestic payout APIs have separate eligibility, funding and regulatory requirements.


##


The Cross-Border Disconnect: Why Native Platform Withdrawals Confuse Indian Freelancers


Freelance marketplaces have their own payment partners. They may not optimise for your local settlement preferences, which means getting payments is as hard as convincing new clients.


When a freelancer sets the “Direct to Local Bank” transfer settings, the platform routes these funds through a network you don’t know anything about. You may lose time and margin.


Choosing SWIFT transfer is another way to lose money and time. You may have to wait 3 to 5 business days just to get your payment, and that too after deducting route-specific fees, such as an illustrative $25 to $50 from the total payment.


Plus, when you account for the FX spread, the damage is higher. Freelance platform default payment systems don’t offer the mid-market rate, and their markup depends on the provider and route.


### Unit Economics of a $10,000 Withdrawal: An Illustrative Comparison


This is illustrative maths, not a provider quote. ₹83.50 is an assumed rate, not a live quote. The benchmark excludes provider fees, platform service fees and taxes. The ₹2,505 wire-fee equivalent uses the assumed benchmark rate.


[Freelancers](https://www.cashfree.com/freelancer-payment-gateway/) and agencies can lose margin on cross-border transfers. Here’s how a $10,000 transfer from a freelance platform to your bank account works;


**Treasury Metric** **Illustrative Platform Withdrawal** **Benchmark Before Provider Fees**


**Gross Invoice Value** $10,000 $10,000


**Assumed Mid-Market Rate** ₹83.50 ₹83.50


**Applied FX Rate** ₹80.58 (3.5% Spread) ₹83.50 (Zero Spread)


**Fixed Wire/Hop Fees** $30 (₹2,505) $0 (₹0)


**Net INR Realised** ₹803,295 ₹835,000


**Difference From Benchmark** ₹31,705 ₹0


In this example, you are losing more than ₹30,000 on a single $10,000 transfer. Why? Spread Markup.


This markup is an additional cost you pay involuntarily on gross revenue. Now multiply this by 5 or 10 invoices of the same amount in a month, and you are losing between ₹1.5 lakhs and ₹3 Lakhs in a month.


##


Compliance Also Matters: GST, FIRC and the Cost of Exporting Services


Losing money to FX spreads hurts your revenue generation, true. But there’s more.


Failing a GST audit hurts more, as it can damage your business and reputation, and then there may be legal issues.


Export of services, defined under Section 2(6) of the Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) Act, is a “zero-rated supply” under Section 16, where all export conditions are met.


This means eligible exporters of services can supply without paying IGST under an LUT or bond, subject to conditions. In other words, you keep the margin, but the law demands strict proof that you are doing business with a foreign entity.


You must prove you received the consideration in convertible foreign exchange, or INR wherever permitted by the RBI. A foreign client alone is insufficient: the supplier, recipient, place of supply and distinct-establishment conditions also matter.


### Local Payout Complexities You Must Manage


Native platform withdrawals may use local settlement partners to speed up delivery. A platform might convert your USD internationally and execute the final mile as a domestic NEFT or IMPS transfer from their local Indian nodal account.


Looks convenient, right?


But this particular method can create a documentation gap. Such domestic transfers may not display SWIFT MT103 remittance data. The final transaction will appear as local INR credit on your bank statement.


GST officers may review these entries and ask for export evidence. Here’s what happens;


- Without an FIRC or an e-FIRA, retain alternative bank and invoice evidence; missing one document does not automatically make this domestic income.
- If export conditions are not met, the applicable domestic GST may be demanded retrospectively.
- They may also add applicable interest and penalties on this amount.


Missing remittance evidence can leave applicable Export Data Processing and Monitoring System (EDPMS) entries open. Chartered Accountants may need the AD bank’s confirmation to[reconcile the books](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/reconciling-your-payment/) . The frictional cost of exporting services skyrockets when teams spend hundreds of manual hours chasing banks for physical FIRCs.

##


How a Platform Running on the PA-CB Framework Supports Cross-Border Collections


Recognising these structural flaws in legacy Online Payment Gateway Service Provider (OPGSP) guidelines, the RBI introduced the Payment Aggregator-Cross Border (PA-CB) framework, now consolidated in its 2025 PA Directions.


The PA-CB regulations enforce strict capital requirements, KYC mandates, and direct central bank supervision.


The new framework has successfully transformed loosely regulated grey areas of transfers into formalised and institutional banking rails.


Recognising this shift in momentum, Cashfree became the first entity in India to secure this PA-CB authorisation from the RBI. We did the hard work for you.


Operating under the PA-CB license gives us the infrastructure to provide the software and the structure you need to receive cross-border payments at lower costs and with support for the required compliance records.


RBI supervises our settlement mechanics, collection account structures, and reporting cadences.


This means you can route supported[cross-border payments](https://www.cashfree.com/cross-border-payment-solutions/) using our rails while staying compliant and reducing operational hurdles along the way.

##


How to Build an Inward Remittance Workflow for Freelancers and Agencies


Freelancers and IT agencies need to build an inward remittance architecture to stay compliant and stop margin leakage. Freelancer platforms don’t provide these settings by default, and you need to know which supported options these systems permit.


### Compare Options Before Letting the Platform Convert Your Currency


Using Cashfree’s Global Collections infrastructure, you can have a dedicated and virtual receiving account outside India.


- You can generate a US routing number and account number for USD, a sort code for GBP, and an IBAN for EUR.
- Having generated these, as per your requirements, you can add these virtual account details into the freelancer platform’s Direct Deposit or ACH withdrawal settings, only where both providers permit the account and the beneficiary details match.
- The platform executes a local transfer in the native currency, subject to platform and provider fees.


On top of this, Cashfree intercepts the funds natively, applies its quoted exchange rate transparently, and routes the net INR value to your Indian current account. Cashfree advertises no forex markup for this product; processing fees and applicable taxes still matter.


### Automated e-FIRA Generation: Download and Match the Invoice


Chasing clients for FIRC manually takes away productive hours and adds to the stress. The supported Cashfree collection workflow can simplify this internally.


When cross-border payments are processed through Cashfree’s infrastructure, you declare and confirm the[correct export purpose code](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/purpose-code-for-international-payments/) for the inward remittance.


Cashfree advertises e-FIRA within 24 hours for supported transactions. You can then complete five critical steps;


- Cashfree automatically generates a digitally signed e-FIRA.
- You download the document directly from the dashboard.
- You forward the PDF to your Chartered Accountant.
- Your AD bank updates applicable EDPMS records after verification.
- Your GST zero-rated export status still depends on meeting all legal conditions.


### Check EEFC Account Integration and Conversion Rules


Freelancers working at volume need advanced treasury tools. They need an EEFC account.


The smart way to convert your currency is not to convert it immediately. An[Exchange Earners’ Foreign Currency (EEFC) account](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/eefc-account/) does not convert foreign currency upon receipt.


Cashfree publishes support for collection into EEFC accounts, subject to onboarding and the approved flow. This means that where Toptal and Cashfree approve payment in USD into the virtual account, the supported flow can route USD directly to your Indian EEFC account without conversion.


For now, you may hold eligible USD receipts, subject to RBI conversion rules.


You will decide when to convert USD into INR, following the macroeconomic indicators and without assuming the conversion always works in your favour. Monthly accruals generally need conversion by the end of the following calendar month after permitted utilisation or commitments.


##


How Marketplaces and HR-Tech Platforms Can Build an Upwork-Like INR Payout Infrastructure


For platform owners, speed is the most important benefit.


Your contractors will demand instant liquidity, and you need to ensure they get it while staying compliant.


Legacy payout structures offer SWIFT wires that are also processed in batches. A marketplace treasury team compiles a CSV file of Indian contractor banking details, uploads it to their corporate bank on Friday afternoon, and prays the funds clear by Tuesday.


These banks can reject transfers due to the smallest errors, like a low character limit in the beneficiary name. Their rejection hurts your reputation and increases the support ticket queue.


Is there a way around this?


### API-Driven Domestic Disbursals After Cross-Border Collection


Start by integrating[Cashfree’s Payout APIs](https://www.cashfree.com/payouts/) to simplify the domestic last-mile process we discussed above. This is not a replacement for the regulated cross-border collection leg.


- After the compliant inbound collection leg, and subject to approved funding, you need to pre-fund a dedicated account and ledger. This architecture operates in real time.
- If a freelancer in Bengaluru clicks on Withdraw, the server fires an API payload to Cashfree, and it instantly debits the pre-funded account.
- This last-mile disbursal sends the money directly into the freelancer’s account through their UPI ID or IMPS bank account.


Following this structure, you can support 24/7 domestic disbursals on eligible rails. Bank downtime,[beneficiary validation](https://www.cashfree.com/bank-account-verification/) and screening can still cause delays. With failure handling and payment tracking, this structure can reduce support tickets. Cashfree converts your back-office administrative burden into a core competitive advantage.


##


Navigating GST Input Tax Credits and Output Liability on Payment Fees


Payment gateways don’t operate for free. And you also need to account for tax obligations. The gateways charge a fee, and tax obligations depend on the transaction and applicable rules.


### GST on Gateway Processing Fees


Cashfree adds 18% GST on the transaction processing fee, and we are obligated to do that as per the rules. Where freelancers consider this as a sunk cost, IT agencies and B2B service exporters may claim eligible Input Tax Credit (ITC), subject to GST conditions.


Consider an agency paying ₹10,000 in gateway fees over a month. Cashfree adds ₹1,800 as GST. Cashfree issues a B2B tax invoice featuring[your GSTIN](https://www.cashfree.com/gst-verification/) . This ₹1,800 can populate in your GSTR-2B statement after correct supplier reporting; reflection alone does not establish eligibility.


### Claim Eligible ITC on Gateway Fees


Utilise the ₹1800 you claimed from ITC to offset eligible output GST you owe. For instance, if you sell software development services and have a GST liability, you can use this ITC to pay the owed taxes.


As an exporter of services, you can exclude e-way bill compliance for pure services supplied without movement of goods. Your tax record-keeping strategy includes these three things;


- Matching B2B gateway invoices
- Claiming ITC
- Maintaining e-FIRAs and the other records supporting zero-rated export status


***Also read:[Input Tax Credit Under GST: Eligibility and Documents](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/input-tax-credit-gst/)***


##


An Illustrative Integration of AI and Agentic Systems for Freelance Payment Remittances


The cross-border payment architecture is evolving, and today many systems still use static API calls. The way forward is Agentic payments.


Static routing forces every transaction down the same rail. So regardless of the external market conditions, all payments go through the same process, and that’s why some payments go through, some are stuck, the margins change from vendor to vendor, and so on.


Agentic systems are changing this reality.


As an illustrative design, a business could implement algorithms that analyse the exact parameters of every withdrawal in real-time. An AI-driven system evaluates;


- Size of the payout
- Current FX market volatility
- Time of the day
- Contractor’s historical urgency


Using these variables and many more, the agent dynamically selects the optimal settlement rail. For instance, if the USD/INR pair shows extreme short-term volatility based on MACD indicators, the agentic protocol might route a massive agency payout through an EEFC hold.


This is a conceptual workflow, not a verified Cashfree feature. EEFC decisions require approved instructions and compliance with RBI limits.


##


Connect Freelance Platforms With Clear Fees and Payment Records


Connecting freelance platforms, marketplaces, and HR payroll platforms to the Indian banking system requires structural precision. You cannot treat cross-border revenue like a simple P2P transfer.


When using the default native platform withdrawals, you may face FX spreads; 3% to 5% is an illustrative assumption, not a universal platform charge. Moreover, accepting localised domestic payouts without adequate remittance evidence can complicate GST compliance; missing SWIFT MT103 data alone does not decide export status.


So, you must take control over the inward remittance flow.


Using the structure already built by a PA-CB licensed platform like Cashfree changes the entire unit economics, offering;


- Reviewing quoted exchange rates and all-in fees for IT agencies and freelancers.
- CA gets available e-FIRAs for supported transactions, alongside the records needed for EDPMS and GST requirements.
- Marketplace founders replace slow and expensive SWIFT batches with real-time API disbursals through UPI and IMPS.

FAQs


#### How can I get an e-FIRA for Upwork or Deel withdrawals to retain my zero-rated GST export status?


For a supported collection flow, you can get an e-FIRA through your PA-CB licensed provider. Cashfree’s Global Collections records inward remittances against your declared and verified export code. Cashfree advertises a digitally signed e-FIRA within 24 hours for supported transactions; confirm eligibility and the other documents needed for zero-rated exports.


#### How can I bypass the 3% to 5% currency conversion spread on freelance platforms?


To protect your margins from being eroded due to FX spreads, compare the default INR withdrawal options. Where supported, you can open a virtual USD, GBP, or EUR receiving account using Cashfree’s Global Collections. Enter these details into your Upwork or Toptal withdrawal window only where approved. Applicable platform and provider fees still apply to the native-currency transfer.


#### Can Indian IT agencies route freelance marketplace payouts directly into an EEFC account?


Where the platform, provider and bank support it, using the payment gateway’s infrastructure, you can route the incoming foreign currency directly to your EEFC account. This means you can hold the USD and execute INR conversion within RBI’s applicable conversion and utilisation rules.


#### Is there a way for HR-tech platforms to disburse INR to Indian contractors without using the SWIFT mode?


Yes, for the domestic last mile after lawful cross-border receipt, you can replace SWIFT wire transfers with API-driven local payouts. As you integrate a payout API and a pre-funded dedicated Indian ledger, it makes the process easier. When an Indian contractor requests a withdrawal, the API instantly debits the ledger and executes the last-mile domestic transfer through UPI or IMPS.
